trs.20: Nūn.<sup foot_note=197586>1</sup> By the pen and what they inscribe,
trs.85: Nun By the pen! By all they write!
trs.22: Nun. By the Pen and the (Record) which (men) write,-
trs.203:
Nûn.
[These letters (Nun, etc.) are one of the miracles of the Qur’an, and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings].
By the pen and by what they (the angels) write (in the Records of men).

trs.20: You are not, [O Muḥammad], by the favor of your Lord, a madman.
trs.85: Your Lord’s grace does not make you [Prophet] a madman:
trs.22: Thou art not, by the Grace of thy Lord, mad or possessed.
trs.203: You (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم), by the Grace of your Lord, are not mad.

trs.20: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted.
trs.85: you will have a never-ending reward––
trs.22: Nay, verily for thee is a Reward unfailing:
trs.203: And Verily, for you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) will be an endless reward.

trs.20: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.
trs.85: truly you have a strong character––
trs.22: And thou (standest) on an exalted standard of character.
trs.203: And Verily, you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) are on an exalted (standard of) character.

trs.20: So you will see and they will see.
trs.85: and soon you will see, as will they,
trs.22: Soon wilt thou see, and they will see,
trs.203: You will see, and they will see,

trs.20: Which of you is the afflicted [by a devil].
trs.85: which of you is afflicted with madness.
trs.22: Which of you is afflicted with madness.
trs.203: Which of you is afflicted with madness.

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ

trs.20: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
trs.85: Your Lord knows best who strays from His path and who is rightly guided.
trs.22: Verily it is thy Lord that knoweth best, which (among men) hath strayed from His Path: and He knoweth best those who receive (true) Guidance.
trs.203: Verily, your Lord is the Best Knower of him who has gone astray from His Path, and He is the Best Knower of those who are guided.

trs.20: Then do not obey the deniers.
trs.85: So do not yield to those who deny the truth––
trs.22: So hearken not to those who deny (the Truth).
trs.203: So (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) obey you not the deniers [(of Islâmic Monotheism - those who belie the Verses of Allâh), the Oneness of Allâh, and the Messengership of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم]<sup foot_note=154996>1</sup>

trs.20: They wish that you would soften [in your position], so they would soften [toward you].
trs.85: they want you to compromise with them and then they will compromise with you––
trs.22: Their desire is that thou shouldst be pliant: so would they be pliant.
trs.203: They wish that you should compromise (in religion out of courtesy) with them: so they (too) would compromise with you.

trs.20: And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer
trs.85: do not yield to any contemptible swearer,
trs.22: Heed not the type of despicable men,- ready with oaths,
trs.203: And (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) obey you not everyone Hallaf Mahîn (the one who swears much and is a liar or is worthless). [Tafsir At-Tabari]

trs.20: [And] scorner, going about with malicious gossip -
trs.85: to any backbiter, slander-monger,
trs.22: A slanderer, going about with calumnies,
trs.203: A slanderer, going about with calumnies,

trs.20: A preventer of good, transgressing and sinful,
trs.85: or hinderer of good, to anyone who is sinful, aggressive,
trs.22: (Habitually) hindering (all) good, transgressing beyond bounds, deep in sin,
trs.203: Hinderer of the good, transgressor, sinful,

trs.20: Cruel, moreover, and an illegitimate pretender.<sup foot_note=197587>1</sup>
trs.85: coarse, and on top of all that, an imposter.
trs.22: Violent (and cruel),- with all that, base-born,-
trs.203: Cruel, and moreover base-born (of illegitimate birth).

trs.20: Because he is a possessor of wealth and children,
trs.85: Just because he has wealth and sons,
trs.22: Because he possesses wealth and (numerous) sons.
trs.203: (He was so) because he had wealth and children.

verses.text_uthmani: إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ ءَايَـٰتُنَا قَالَ أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ

trs.20: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."
trs.85: when our revelations are recited to him, he says, ‘These are just ancient fables.’
trs.22: When to him are rehearsed Our Signs, "Tales of the ancients", he cries!
trs.203: When Our Verses (of the Qur’ân) are recited to him, he says: "Tales of the men of old!"

trs.20: We will brand him upon the snout.<sup foot_note=197588>1</sup>
trs.85: We shall brand him on the snout!
trs.22: Soon shall We brand (the beast) on the snout!
trs.203: We shall brand him on the snout (nose)!

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّا بَلَوْنَـٰهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَآ أَصْحَـٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا۟ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ

trs.20: Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut its fruit in the [early] morning
trs.85: We have tried them as We tried the owners of a certain garden, who swore that they would harvest its fruits in the morning
trs.22: Verily We have tried them as We tried the People of the Garden, when they resolved to gather the fruits of the (garden) in the morning.
trs.203: Verily, We have tried them as We tried the people of the garden, when they swore to pluck the fruits of the (garden) in the morning,

trs.20: Without making exception.<sup foot_note=197589>1</sup>
trs.85: and made no allowance [for the Will of God]:
trs.22: But made no reservation, ("If it be Allah's Will").
trs.203: Without saying: Inshâ’ Allâh (If Allâh wills).

verses.text_uthmani: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ

trs.20: So there came upon it [i.e., the garden] an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep.
trs.85: a disaster from your Lord struck the garden as they slept
trs.22: Then there came on the (garden) a visitation from thy Lord, (which swept away) all around, while they were asleep.
trs.203: Then there passed by on the (garden) a visitation (fire) from your Lord at night and burnt it while they were asleep.

trs.20: And it became as though reaped.
trs.85: and by morning it was stripped bare, a desolate land.
trs.22: So the (garden) became, by the morning, like a dark and desolate spot, (whose fruit had been gathered).
trs.203: So the (garden) became black by the morning, like a pitch dark night (in complete ruins).

trs.20: And they called one another at morning,
trs.85: Still they called each other at daybreak,
trs.22: As the morning broke, they called out, one to another,-
trs.203: Then they called out one to another as soon as the morning broke.

verses.text_uthmani: أَنِ ٱغْدُوا۟ عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰرِمِينَ

trs.20: [Saying], "Go early to your crop if you would cut the fruit."
trs.85: ‘Go early to your field if you wish to gather all its fruits,’
trs.22: "Go ye to your tilth (betimes) in the morning, if ye would gather the fruits."
trs.203: Saying: "Go to your tilth in the morning, if you would pluck the fruits."

trs.20: So they set out, while lowering their voices,
trs.85: and went off, whispering,
trs.22: So they departed, conversing in secret low tones, (saying)-
trs.203: So they departed, conversing in secret low tones (saying):

verses.text_uthmani: أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌ

trs.20: [Saying], "There will surely not enter it today upon you [any] poor person."
trs.85: ‘Make sure no poor person enters the garden today!’––
trs.22: "Let not a single indigent person break in upon you into the (garden) this day."
trs.203: "No Miskîn (poor man) shall enter upon you into it today."

trs.20: And they went early in determination, [assuming themselves] able.<sup foot_note=197590>1</sup>
trs.85: they left early, bent on their purpose-
trs.22: And they opened the morning, strong in an (unjust) resolve.
trs.203: And they went in the morning with strong intention, thinking that they have power (to prevent the poor taking anything of the fruits therefrom).

trs.20: But when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we are lost;
trs.85: but when they saw the garden, they said, ‘We must have lost our way!
trs.22: But when they saw the (garden), they said: "We have surely lost our way:
trs.203: But when they saw the (garden), they said: "Verily, we have gone astray."

trs.20: Rather, we have been deprived."
trs.85: No- we are ruined!’
trs.22: "Indeed we are shut out (of the fruits of our labour)!"
trs.203: (Then they said): "Nay! Indeed we are deprived of (the fruits)!"

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ

trs.20: The most moderate of them said, "Did I not say to you, 'Why do you not exalt [Allāh]?'"<sup foot_note=197591>1</sup>
trs.85: The wisest of them said, ‘Did I not say to you, “Will you not glorify God?”’-
trs.22: Said one of them, more just (than the rest): "Did I not say to you, 'Why not glorify (Allah)?'"
trs.203: The best among them said: "Did I not tell you: why say you not: Inshâ’ Allâh (If Allâh wills)."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَـٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَـٰلِمِينَ

trs.20: They said, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
trs.85: they said, ‘Glory be to God, Our Lord! Truly, we were doing wrong!’-
trs.22: They said: "Glory to our Lord! Verily we have been doing wrong!"
trs.203: They said: "Glory to Our Lord! Verily, we have been Zâlimûn (wrong-doers)."

trs.20: Then they approached one another, blaming each other.
trs.85: and then they turned to each other in mutual reproach.
trs.22: Then they turned, one against another, in reproach.
trs.203: Then they turned one against another, blaming.

trs.20: They said, "O woe to us; indeed we were transgressors.
trs.85: They said, ‘Alas for us! We have done terrible wrong,
trs.22: They said: "Alas for us! We have indeed transgressed!
trs.203: They said: "Woe to us! Verily, we were Tâghûn (transgressors and disobedient)

verses.text_uthmani: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ

trs.20: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us [one] better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous."<sup foot_note=197592>1</sup>
trs.85: but maybe our Lord will give us something better in its place: we truly turn to Him in hope.’
trs.22: "It may be that our Lord will give us in exchange a better (garden) than this: for we do turn to Him (in repentance)!"
trs.203: We hope that our Lord will give us in exchange a better (garden) than this. Truly, we turn to our Lord (wishing for good that He may forgive our sins and reward us in the Hereafter).

verses.text_uthmani: كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْعَذَابُ ۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ

trs.20: Such is the punishment [of this world]. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
trs.85: Such is the punishment [in this life], but greater still is the punishment in the Hereafter, if only they knew.
trs.22: Such is the Punishment (in this life); but greater is the Punishment in the Hereafter,- if only they knew!
trs.203: Such is the punishment (in this life), but truly, the punishment of the Hereafter is greater if they but knew.

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّـٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ

trs.20: Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are the Gardens of Pleasure.
trs.85: There will be Gardens of bliss for those who are mindful of God.
trs.22: Verily, for the Righteous, are Gardens of Delight, in the Presence of their Lord.
trs.203: Verily, for the Muttaqûn (the pious - See V.2:2) are Gardens of delight (Paradise) with their Lord.

trs.20: Then will We treat the Muslims like the criminals?
trs.85: Should We treat those who submit to Us as We treat those who do evil?
trs.22: Shall We then treat the People of Faith like the People of Sin?
trs.203: Shall We then treat the Muslims (believers of Islamic Monotheism, doers of righteous deeds) like the Mujrimûn (criminals, polytheists and disbelievers, etc.)?

trs.20: What is [the matter] with you? How do you judge?
trs.85: What is the matter with you? On what basis do you judge?
trs.22: What is the matter with you? How judge ye?
trs.203: What is the matter with you? How judge you?

trs.20: Or do you have a scripture in which you learn
trs.85: Do you have a Scripture that tells you
trs.22: Or have ye a book through which ye learn-
trs.203: Or have you a Book wherein you learn,

trs.20: That indeed for you is whatever you choose?
trs.85: that you will be granted whatever you choose?
trs.22: That ye shall have, through it whatever ye choose?
trs.203: That you shall therein have all that you choose?

verses.text_uthmani: أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَـٰنٌ عَلَيْنَا بَـٰلِغَةٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ ۙ إِنَّ لَكُمْ لَمَا تَحْكُمُونَ

trs.20: Or do you have oaths [binding] upon Us, extending until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed for you is whatever you judge?
trs.85: Have you received from Us solemn oaths, binding to the Day of Resurrection, that you will get whatever you yourselves decide?
trs.22: Or have ye Covenants with Us to oath, reaching to the Day of Judgment, (providing) that ye shall have whatever ye shall demand?
trs.203: Or have you oaths from Us, reaching to the Day of Resurrection, that yours will be what you judge?

trs.20: Ask them which of them, for that [claim], is responsible.
trs.85: Ask them [Prophet] which of them will guarantee this.
trs.22: Ask thou of them, which of them will stand surety for that!
trs.203: Ask them, which of them will stand surety for that!

verses.text_uthmani: أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فَلْيَأْتُوا۟ بِشُرَكَآئِهِمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ صَـٰدِقِينَ

trs.20: Or do they have partners?<sup foot_note=197593>1</sup> Then let them bring their partners, if they should be truthful.
trs.85: Do they have ‘partners’ [besides God]? Let them produce their ‘partners’, if what they say is true.
trs.22: Or have they some “ Partners ” (in Godhead)? Then let them produce Their “ partners ”,  If they are truthful !
trs.203: Or have they "partners"? Then let them bring their "partners" if they are truthful!

verses.text_uthmani: يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَن سَاقٍ وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ

trs.20: The Day the shin will be uncovered<sup foot_note=197594>1</sup> and they are invited to prostration but they [i.e., the disbelievers] will not be able,
trs.85: On the Day when matters become dire, they will be invited to prostrate themselves but will be prevented from doing so,
trs.22: The Day that the shin shall be laid bare, and they shall be summoned to bow in adoration, but they shall not be able,-
trs.203: (Remember) the Day when the Shin<sup foot_note=154997>1</sup> shall be laid bare (i.e. the Day of Resurrection) and they shall be called to prostrate themselves (to Allâh), but they (hypocrites) shall not be able to do so.

verses.text_uthmani: خَـٰشِعَةً أَبْصَـٰرُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ ۖ وَقَدْ كَانُوا۟ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَـٰلِمُونَ

trs.20: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. And they used to be invited to prostration while they were sound.<sup foot_note=197595>1</sup>
trs.85: and their eyes will be downcast and they will be overwhelmed with shame: they were invited to prostrate themselves when they were safe [but refused].
trs.22: Their eyes will be cast down,- ignominy will cover them; seeing that they had been summoned aforetime to bow in adoration, while they were whole, (and had refused).
trs.203: Their eyes will be cast down and ignominy will cover them; they used to be called to prostrate themselves (offer prayers), while they were healthy and good (in the life of the world, but they did not).

verses.text_uthmani: فَذَرْنِى وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ ۖ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُم مِّنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

trs.20: So leave Me, [O Muḥammad], with [the matter of] whoever denies this statement [i.e., the Qur’ān]. We will progressively lead them [to punishment] from where they do not know.<sup foot_note=197596>1</sup>
trs.85: So [Prophet] leave those who reject this revelation to Me: We shall lead them on, step by step, in ways beyond their knowledge;
trs.22: Then leave Me alone with such as reject this Message: by degrees shall We punish them from directions they perceive not.
trs.203: Then leave Me Alone with such as belie this Qur’ân. We shall punish them gradually from directions they perceive not.

trs.20: And I will give them time. Indeed, My plan is firm.
trs.85: I will allow them more time, for My plan is powerful.
trs.22: A (long) respite will I grant them: truly powerful is My Plan.
trs.203: And I will grant them a respite. Verily, My Plan is strong.

verses.text_uthmani: أَمْ تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ أَجْرًا فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ

trs.20: Or do you ask of them a payment, so they are by debt burdened down?
trs.85: Do you demand some reward from them that would burden them with debt?
trs.22: Or is it that thou dost ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with a load of debt?-
trs.203: Or is it that you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) ask them a wage, so that they are heavily burdened with debt?

trs.20: Or have they [knowledge of] the unseen, so they write [it] down?
trs.85: Do they have knowledge of the unseen that enables them to write it down?
trs.22: Or that the Unseen is in their hands, so that they can write it down?
trs.203: Or that the Ghaib (the Unseen - here in this Verse it means Al-Lauh Al-Mahfûz) is in their hands, so that they can write it down?

verses.text_uthmani: فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ

trs.20: Then be patient for the decision of your Lord, [O Muḥammad], and be not like the companion of the fish [i.e., Jonah] when he called out while he was distressed.
trs.85: Wait patiently [Prophet] for your Lord’s judgement: do not be like the man in the whale who called out in distress:
trs.22: So wait with patience for the Command of thy Lord, and be not like the Companion of the Fish,- when he cried out in agony.
trs.203: So wait with patience for the Decision of your Lord, and be not like the Companion of the Fish - when he cried out (to Us) while he was in deep sorrow. (See the Qur’ân, Verse 21:87).

verses.text_uthmani: لَّوْلَآ أَن تَدَٰرَكَهُۥ نِعْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ

trs.20: If not that a favor [i.e., mercy] from his Lord overtook him, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was censured.<sup foot_note=197597>1</sup>
trs.85: if his Lord’s grace had not reached him, he would have been left, abandoned and blameworthy, on the barren shore,
trs.22: Had not Grace from his Lord reached him, he would indeed have been cast off on the naked shore, in disgrace.
trs.203: Had not a Grace from his Lord reached him, he would indeed have been (left in the stomach of the fish, but We forgave him): so he was cast off on the naked shore, while he was to be blamed.

translation.text: surely he would have been thrown

trs.20: And his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous.
trs.85: but his Lord chose him and made him one of the Righteous.
trs.22: Thus did his Lord choose him and make him of the Company of the Righteous.
trs.203: Then his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous.

verses.text_uthmani: وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَـٰرِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا۟ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُۥ لَمَجْنُونٌ

trs.20: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes [i.e., looks] when they hear the message, and they say, "Indeed, he is mad."
trs.85: The disbelievers almost strike you down with their looks when they hear the Quran. They say, ‘He must be mad!’
trs.22: And the Unbelievers would almost trip thee up with their eyes when they hear the Message; and they say: "Surely he is possessed!"
trs.203: And verily, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes (through hatred) when they hear the Reminder (the Qur’ân), and they say: "Verily, he (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) is a madman!"

trs.20: But it is not except a reminder to the worlds.
trs.85: but truly it is nothing other than a Reminder for all peoples.
trs.22: But it is nothing less than a Message to all the worlds.
trs.203: But it is nothing else than a Reminder to all the ‘Âlamîn (mankind, and jinn).
